reply: Grocery Fan Appreciation Day had the highest peak live audience this year, with 15,805 viewers. It was hosted by Nicole Mack.

WITH campaign_peaks AS (
  SELECT c.campaign_id, c.name AS campaign_name, h.name AS host_name,
         MAX(m.peak_concurrent_viewers) AS peak_live_audience
  FROM campaigns c
  JOIN departments d ON d.department_id = c.department_id
  LEFT JOIN hosts h ON h.host_id = c.host_id
  JOIN campaign_metrics m ON m.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
  WHERE d.name = 'Fresh Grocery'
    AND c.start_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND c.start_date < DATE '2027-01-01'
  GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.name, h.name
)
SELECT campaign_name, host_name, peak_live_audience
FROM campaign_peaks
WHERE peak_live_audience = (SELECT MAX(peak_live_audience) FROM campaign_peaks)
ORDER BY campaign_name

question: Why did Grocery Black Friday Live hit its GMV and audience targets but miss conversion and go over budget?
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, c.start_date, c.planned_operating_cost, c.actual_operating_cost, SUM(m.gmv) AS gmv, AVG(m.conversion_rate) AS conversion_rate, MAX(m.peak_concurrent_viewers) AS peak_concurrent_viewers FROM campaigns c JOIN departments d ON d.department_id = c.department_id JOIN campaign_metrics m ON m.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE d.name = 'Fresh Grocery' AND c.name = 'Grocery Black Friday Live' AND c.start_date = DATE '2025-11-12' GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.name, c.start_date, c.planned_operating_cost, c.actual_operating_cost
reply: The campaign drew 16,069 summed daily audience and generated $181,056.65 GMV, but average conversion was 8.84%; product click-through averaged 15.8%, with especially low rates for Instant Ramen (5.97%) and Snow Crab Legs (7.15%), suggesting a weaker product-to-purchase funnel despite the reach. It spent $34,027.23 against a $28,866.58 plan—$5,160.65 over—but the available data has no cost breakdown to explain what drove the overspend.

WITH target_campaign AS (
  SELECT c.campaign_id, c.name, c.planned_operating_cost, c.actual_operating_cost
  FROM campaigns c
  JOIN departments d ON d.department_id = c.department_id
  WHERE d.name = 'Fresh Grocery'
    AND c.name = 'Grocery Black Friday Live'
), metric_summary AS (
  SELECT m.campaign_id,
         COUNT(*) AS metric_days,
         SUM(m.gmv) AS total_gmv,
         SUM(m.dau) AS summed_daily_audience,
         ROUND(AVG(m.conversion_rate), 4) AS avg_conversion_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(m.watch_time), 2) AS avg_watch_time,
         ROUND(AVG(m.avg_dwell_time_minutes), 2) AS avg_dwell_minutes,
         SUM(m.peak_concurrent_viewers) AS summed_peak_concurrent_viewers
  FROM campaign_metrics m
  JOIN target_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = m.campaign_id
  GROUP BY m.campaign_id
), product_summary AS (
  SELECT p.campaign_id,
         SUM(p.units_sold) AS total_units_sold,
         SUM(p.sales_amount) AS product_sales_amount,
         ROUND(AVG(p.click_through_rate), 4) AS avg_product_click_through_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(p.sell_through_rate), 4) AS avg_sell_through_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(p.return_rate), 4) AS avg_return_rate,
         SUM(p.profit) AS total_product_profit,
         jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('product', p.product_name, 'units_sold', p.units_sold,
           'sales_amount', p.sales_amount, 'click_through_rate', p.click_through_rate,
           'sell_through_rate', p.sell_through_rate, 'return_rate', p.return_rate,
           'profit', p.profit) ORDER BY p.sales_amount DESC) AS products
  FROM campaign_products p
  JOIN target_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = p.campaign_id
  GROUP BY p.campaign_id
), behavior_summary AS (
  SELECT b.campaign_id,
         COUNT(*) AS customer_records,
         ROUND(AVG(b.dwell_time_minutes), 2) AS avg_customer_dwell_minutes,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.purchase_amount > 0) AS purchasing_customer_records,
         ROUND(AVG(b.purchase_amount) FILTER (WHERE b.purchase_amount > 0), 2) AS avg_purchase_amount,
         jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('region', b.region, 'dwell_minutes', b.dwell_time_minutes,
                                     'purchase_amount', b.purchase_amount)) AS behavior_records
  FROM campaign_customer_behavior b
  JOIN target_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = b.campaign_id
  GROUP BY b.campaign_id
)
SELECT c.name, c.planned_operating_cost, c.actual_operating_cost,
       c.actual_operating_cost - c.planned_operating_cost AS cost_overrun,
       ms.total_gmv, ms.summed_daily_audience, ms.avg_conversion_rate,
       ms.avg_watch_time, ms.avg_dwell_minutes, ms.metric_days,
       ps.total_units_sold, ps.product_sales_amount, ps.avg_product_click_through_rate,
       ps.avg_sell_through_rate, ps.avg_return_rate, ps.total_product_profit, ps.products,
       bs.customer_records, bs.avg_customer_dwell_minutes, bs.purchasing_customer_records,
       bs.avg_purchase_amount, bs.behavior_records
FROM target_campaign c
LEFT JOIN metric_summary ms ON ms.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN product_summary ps ON ps.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN behavior_summary bs ON bs.campaign_id = c.campaign_id;

WITH target_campaign AS (
  SELECT c.campaign_id, c.name, c.planned_operating_cost, c.actual_operating_cost
  FROM campaigns c
  JOIN departments d ON d.department_id = c.department_id
  WHERE d.name = 'Fresh Grocery'
    AND c.name = 'Grocery Black Friday Live'
), metric_summary AS (
  SELECT m.campaign_id,
         COUNT(*) AS metric_days,
         SUM(m.gmv) AS total_gmv,
         SUM(m.dau) AS summed_daily_audience,
         ROUND(AVG(m.conversion_rate), 4) AS avg_conversion_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(m.watch_time), 2) AS avg_watch_time,
         ROUND(AVG(m.avg_dwell_time_minutes), 2) AS avg_dwell_minutes,
         SUM(m.peak_concurrent_viewers) AS summed_peak_concurrent_viewers
  FROM campaign_metrics m
  JOIN target_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = m.campaign_id
  GROUP BY m.campaign_id
), product_summary AS (
  SELECT p.campaign_id,
         SUM(p.units_sold) AS total_units_sold,
         SUM(p.sales_amount) AS product_sales_amount,
         ROUND(AVG(p.click_through_rate), 4) AS avg_product_click_through_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(p.sell_through_rate), 4) AS avg_sell_through_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(p.return_rate), 4) AS avg_return_rate,
         SUM(p.profit) AS total_product_profit,
         jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('product', p.product_name, 'units_sold', p.units_sold,
           'sales_amount', p.sales_amount, 'click_through_rate', p.click_through_rate,
           'sell_through_rate', p.sell_through_rate, 'return_rate', p.return_rate,
           'profit', p.profit) ORDER BY p.sales_amount DESC) AS products
  FROM campaign_products p
  JOIN target_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = p.campaign_id
  GROUP BY p.campaign_id
), behavior_summary AS (
  SELECT b.campaign_id,
         COUNT(*) AS customer_records,
         ROUND(AVG(b.dwell_time_minutes), 2) AS avg_customer_dwell_minutes,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.purchase_amount > 0) AS purchasing_customer_records,
         ROUND(AVG(b.purchase_amount) FILTER (WHERE b.purchase_amount > 0), 2) AS avg_purchase_amount,
         jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('region', b.region, 'dwell_minutes', b.dwell_time_minutes,
                                     'purchase_amount', b.purchase_amount)) AS behavior_records
  FROM campaign_customer_behavior b
  JOIN target_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = b.campaign_id
  GROUP BY b.campaign_id
)
SELECT c.name, c.planned_operating_cost, c.actual_operating_cost,
       c.actual_operating_cost - c.planned_operating_cost AS cost_overrun,
       ms.total_gmv, ms.summed_daily_audience, ms.avg_conversion_rate,
       ms.avg_watch_time, ms.avg_dwell_minutes, ms.metric_days,
       ps.total_units_sold, ps.product_sales_amount, ps.avg_product_click_through_rate,
       ps.avg_sell_through_rate, ps.avg_return_rate, ps.total_product_profit, ps.products,
       bs.customer_records, bs.avg_customer_dwell_minutes, bs.purchasing_customer_records,
       bs.avg_purchase_amount, bs.behavior_records
FROM target_campaign c
LEFT JOIN metric_summary ms ON ms.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN product_summary ps ON ps.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN behavior_summary bs ON bs.campaign_id = c.campaign_id;

reply:
The Beauty Fan Appreciation Day campaign ran Feb 14–Mar 22: operating cost was **$155,117.55**, **$10,763.47 (7.46%) over** its $144,354.08 plan. No planned ROI is recorded; using product profit less operating cost, estimated ROI was **59.6%** (assuming product profit is before operating costs), while GMV was $766,115.13, or **4.94×** operating cost.

Before the next one, confirm whether the plan and results should cover the full 37-day campaign or just event day, agree on the ROI definition and target, and reconcile GMV ($766,115) with product sales ($608,887) and recorded customer purchases ($23,890); also review the **10.7% return rate** and **55.2% sell-through**.

reply: The campaign appears to have converted a relatively modest audience effectively: average conversion was 8.82%, and it sold 3,096 units for $472,533 in product sales ($587,612 GMV), with average customer dwell time of about 25 minutes. question: For the Jan 18 launch, how did the product mix help sales land on target, and what product issues still need attention?
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, c.start_date, mt.gmv, p.product_name, p.sales_amount, p.profit, p.return_rate FROM campaigns c JOIN departments d ON d.department_id = c.department_id JOIN campaign_products p ON p.campaign_id = c.campaign_id JOIN (SELECT campaign_id, SUM(gmv) AS gmv FROM campaign_metrics GROUP BY campaign_id) mt ON mt.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE d.name = 'Home Goods' AND c.name = 'Home New Product Launch' AND c.start_date = DATE '2026-01-18' ORDER BY p.sales_amount DESC
reply:
Paper towels led the Jan 18 launch with **$175.0K in sales** and **90.9% sell-through**; trash bags added another strong performer at **94.3% sell-through** and a **53.3% margin**. Together, they gave the mix a high-volume, profitable backbone. The campaign recorded **$587.6K in GMV**, but the available data has no sales-target figure, so I can’t verify that it landed exactly on target.

Attention is needed on **storage bins** and **laundry detergent**, whose sell-through was only **24.3%** and **28.9%**, respectively. Returns are elevated across the listed products (about **10–13%**), highest for **insulated tumblers at 12.6%**.
